research_rationale: Executive Order 13915 of April 14, 2020 (85 FR 21733), Providing an Order of Succession Within the Department of the Interior, is a four-section order. The held Federal Register text layer (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_13915.txt, 85 FR 21733, PDF pages 1-2) carries the heading, the date April 14, 2020 and the FR Doc. 2020-08392 line, so the identity matches the register row. Section 1 makes the officers named in section 2 act as Secretary of the Interior, subject to section 3, when both the Secretary and the Deputy Secretary of the Interior have died, resigned or are otherwise unable to perform the duties. Section 2 lists seven officers in order. Section 3(a) provides that no officer serving in a listed office in an acting capacity acts as Secretary by virtue of that service, and section 3(b) keeps the President's discretion, to the extent the Vacancies Reform Act permits, to designate an acting Secretary differently. Section 4 revokes Executive Order 13244 of December 18, 2001, and that command was executed when the order was signed on April 14, 2020. The order states no expiry date, event or condition. Its commands are conditional (they apply only when the offices of Secretary and Deputy Secretary are both unavailable), but a condition that has not occurred does not end a command. A search of the held corpus for the number EO 13915 finds only the order's own Federal Register page and the Federal Register copy of FR Doc. 2020-08392; no later order, notice or regulation held cites it, and the three bounded searches report no hit that amends, revokes or supersedes it. The status on 2026-10-14 is operative for the section 1 to 3 commands and the enacting lead, and terminated by performance on 2020-04-14 for section 4. The authority statute's text is not held; this is disclosed in the legal basis, and nothing held shows that the statute was repealed or expired.
savings_reason: Section 4's revocation of Executive Order 13244 was executed when the order was signed on April 14, 2020 and is not undone by any held instrument, so the earlier succession order stays revoked independently of whether sections 1 to 3 continue; the section 2 succession list that replaced it is itself operative on 2026-10-14.
earlier_end_check: The order states no end date, event or condition. Its only dated statements are the signing date April 14, 2020 and the Federal Register filing line, neither of which ends anything. A search of the held corpus for the number EO 13915 (jobs/*/output/texts, excluding clause drafts) finds only the order's own Federal Register page and the Federal Register copy of FR Doc. 2020-08392, so no later order, notice or regulation that revokes, supersedes or amends it is held. The OFR catalog search records no disposition note, the eCFR/CFR search found no regulation naming the order, and the only U.S. Code lead is a 2025-01-06 Table IV listing line. The section 3 exceptions and the conditional wording of section 1 limit when an officer acts; they do not end a command.
scope_check: No later instrument touches any section. Section 4 revoked a different order (Executive Order 13244), and a revocation of that order does not reach this one. Each section is decided on its own text: sections 1 to 3 are standing rules for a future vacancy and remain operative, and section 4 is a completed one-time command.
independent_command_check: The independent commands are: the enacting lead citing the Vacancies Reform Act; the section 1 command that listed officers act as Secretary when both the Secretary and Deputy Secretary are unavailable; the section 2 list of seven offices in order (each lettered paragraph is decided separately); section 3(a) excluding officers serving in an acting capacity; section 3(b) preserving presidential discretion to depart from the list; and the section 4 revocation of Executive Order 13244. Sections 2 and 3 are dependent on section 1's trigger but are separate propositions.
savings_check: Only section 4 is terminated. Its effect, the revocation of Executive Order 13244, was complete when it was signed and survives as the continuing absence of that order; no pending proceeding or accrued right depends on it. Sections 1 to 3 continue, so there is nothing to transfer.
